sections.overall: Double or Nothing '26 is currently rated as the best AEW PPV of all time (9.66)! Whether you agree with that or not, I thought it was a phenomenal event and the match quality backs this up. There were various wrestler gains with some all time peaks, a few returns and a shuffle up in the Men's Rankings. The best match of the week, including the weekly Dynamite and Collision shows was Konosuke Takeshita vs Kazuchika Okada (9.52). A far-better match than their one at Worlds End '25 and a memorable International Title change. MOTY contender, for sure!
sections.mens: Darby vs MJF for the World Title was an excellent match (rated 8.99) and led to gains for both, though two the most notable points-gainers were Takeshita and Okada. Jon Moxley slips back a few spots - the lowest he has been this year - after two solid but unspectacular matches against Kyle O'Reilly (both rated in the 7s).  Another highlight of the week was on Dynamite: Mark Briscoe vs Tommaso Ciampa (8.5). Other highly-rated matches at Double or Nothing have caused some real changes in the Men's ranking positions.It will be fascinating to see how these evolve over the coming weeks.
sections.womens: The devastating news is that Willow Nightingale not only has to relinquish her TBS Title and spot in the Owen Hart Tournament, but her indefinite injury leaves a real void in the Women's Division. We hope your recovery goes OK Willow! The two featured matches on Double or Nothing showed a few small gains, though neither of these were given the same spotlight as the Men's Division (no changes there...). That's why there were no major changes in the rankings.  Hopefully with the Owen Hart tournament underway, this will lead to some opportunities for the women to be given a much-deserved spotlight.
sections.menstag: Plenty of Tag action this week! The biggest of which was the strong World Tag Team Titles match between Cage & Copeland and FTR (8.24), which opened Double or Nothing. The new champs are now at an all team peak rating and ranking of #3. Will they climb any higher than this? Elsewhere, the Stadium Stampede 14 Man Tag was a showcase of various teams; the high rating given (though personally higher than I thought it deserved, at 8.4) led to lots of gains.
sections.womenstag: It's almost getting redundant now to bemoan the lack of spotlight on this division. Hopefully more teams will join soon so that Divine Dominion have some actual competition. Sisters Of Sin still lead the rankings, despite their slight loss in points in the 6 Woman Tag match on Dynamite.
sections.trios: Welcome back to The Elite to the Trios rankings! As part of the Stadium Stampede match, they re-enter at straight at #2, having already had a rating above 100 whilst inactive. They come in just below The Demand, who are at their all time of peak, nearly joing the 120 club!
